signs: Tiny holes and white or yellowish streaks along the leaf edges of young plants
Twisted leaves that break easily in the wind
Stunted plants with fewer tillers; many plants recover as they grow
actions: Check young plants in the first weeks after transplanting, especially where the water stands
Keep the field from standing water for long periods, following local water-management advice
Protect the small wasps, flies, and spiders that feed on the maggots and flies by avoiding unnecessary sprays
callExpertIf: Many young plants are stunted or the damage keeps spreading after the plants should have recovered

insect.stageNote: from seedling to tillering, where the water stands
biological: Small wasps that attack the eggs and maggots
Long-legged flies that eat the eggs
